title: nolan sets up nolan
$comment: The meta-demo: nolan filming the experience of setting up and using nolan, end to end — setup terminal → first run → it films your real app → the final GIF. nolan only films web pages, so 'setup' is a mock terminal (examples/site/setup.html) that nolan types into and `call submit` commits; the 'real app' scene is the actual toy app (index.html); the result scene (done.html) shows a real nolan GIF. Deliberately avoids the purple `pill` caption style. Film with --style=examples/metademo.style.json (presenter is ~20% smaller here).

beats.text: Setting up nolan takes about a minute. Here's the whole thing.
npm i playwright && npx playwright install chromium
Add the browser it films with.

beats.text: Run it, and you get a menu.
Captions, a presenter, cuts and subtitles come built in.
Pick a demo, and nolan drives your actual app.
Change the UI, and the demo breaks in CI — not in front of users.
nolan verify catches drift — gate your build, or just get a heads-up.
Out comes a GIF — and it never goes stale.
Show, don't tell. This demo just set nolan up to make itself.
